samples.question: Two straight dark gray lines split this image into four equal quadrants. Each quadrant contains one wide vertical gray band and exactly one coloured rod that runs behind that band, so only the rod's left piece and its right piece are visible; the light gray squares are scatter and belong to no rod. In exactly one quadrant the two visible pieces are the two ends of a single straight rod, so the left piece's centre line continues exactly into the right piece. In every other quadrant the right piece is shifted parallel to that continuation or hinged away from it, and its centre line departs from the continuation by at least nine pixels on average. Inside a quadrant both pieces always share one colour and one thickness, so colour and thickness never mark the answer, and rod colour, rod thickness, rod tilt, band width, band position, rod height, the number of gray squares and the amount of ink in a quadrant carry no information about which rod is the straight one. Which quadrant holds the rod whose two pieces continue straight through the band? Answer with exactly one of: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.
